kernel: the host-side speculative round: DFlash/MTP block caps, the round-cost table, the depth planners (EV + width chooser), prompt-lookup drafting, tree-round copy, and the acceptance rules
summary: The host round around the verify kernels, not a kernel itself: a drafter chain (or lookup or tree) plus a 1+m-row verify runs once per host touch, and a measured (verify width, KV bucket) round-cost table plus a piecewise fitted surface drive an expected-tokens-per-cost depth plan capped per silicon. Acceptance is exact by default (greedy argmax run; Leviathan rejection when sampled; keyed Gumbel-max under a row-exact trunk with a DFlash drafter, which makes drafted output byte-identical to serial), with opt-in lossy Typical/TokenV3 modes. Lookup rounds are gated per round on measured tokens per cost and never feed the EV acceptance state or the width grid.

gates.condition: Tree round: selector present and enabled, no Markov drafter, request greedy or keyed-serial, tree supported, no sparse-target policy
Tree-round copy: the context backs a continuation matching all tree nodes with >= 24 matching tokens, so the round verifies it as the chain with no assistant forward
Lookup gate: n-gram match with suffix >= 8 and lookup tokens-per-cost beats the MTP chain's; cap 7, or 14 when the suffix >= 16
Lookup rounds always take exact acceptance: a copied point-mass draft under a lossy rule makes copying the context certain and the output loops
A lookup round never feeds the EV acceptance EMAs or the grouped planner, and neither does the MTP round after one (times_round false for both)
updateMtpEvRound and mtpPlannerObserve run only when the round was not a lookup round
Lookup rounds price only the table's separate lookup row (observeLookup), never the width grid
Byte-exact serial acceptance on: request keyed (row-exact config + Metal kernels available), temperature > 0.01, seed set
mtp_serial_accept on: MTP active and config is row-exact and acceptance mode is exact
Greedy acceptance: longest run of verify argmax equalities against the drafts
Sampled acceptance: Leviathan ratio min(1, p/q); greedy-forced drafts keep the one-hot rule min(1, target_p)
Keyed verify rows: under mtp_serial_accept each row is sampled with the serial sampler's key at its own position instead of argmax; drafts survive only when they equal that draw
Runtime acceptance gate: per-draft rate below 0.50 after 5 attempts disables speculation for the rest of the request; never re-enabled within a request
EV base depth: m_lo = argmax over single-chunk depths of expected tokens / round cost, with the standing base held unless a challenger beats it by SWITCH_MARGIN
EV extension: extend while the conditional chain product exceeds best_r * marginal cost; tau = clamp(best_r * t_sum / s_sum, 0.05, 0.95)
Base-depth climb damped: the planner is capped at last round's m_lo + 1 (m_lo_max); demotions are never damped

Trusted-width climb: the per-silicon cap row is a cold-start cap; the plan may exceed it only up to the widest TRUSTED width the table holds (never onto the prior's guess), and the width trial may reach one past that
Depth cap by cost profile: generic -> per-silicon row (default 6), calibrated NAX surfaces -> 8, dense 27B q4/gs64 and qwen4 surfaces -> 6
Round-cost feed: solo rounds only, no width transition, bad samples and self-spikes and step-implausible rounds dropped
Table replaces the prior once a bucket has MIN_WIDTHS = 1 trusted width; lookup row and serial row never reach the width grid

Block drafter width chooser: argmax over widths 0..max of measured tokens per ms, serial (0) a candidate like any other but never trialled; the one unmeasured candidate is widest+1 priced from the acceptance chain and the last measured slope
Serial fallback for a block drafter: serial wins only where a serial round was measured and beats the chain rate by SWITCH_MARGIN
Depth policy switch: single-chunk .accept planner serves KV < 8192; the legacy confidence-gated planner takes over at or above it
Tree block cap: blockCapForMachine returns 8 for any tree round regardless of chip
Wide verify lane: NAX m16 tile present and enabled keeps the checkpoint's configured block instead of the no-lane cap

measured.conditions: DFlash block sweep, 160-token generations, serial reference 28.2 tok/s in the same boot; full ladder: block 16 0.92x, 8 1.16x, 7 1.43x, 6 1.79x, 5 1.97x, 4 1.81x, 3 1.77x
draft-head A/B, 160-token generations, same serial reference: trunk head 57.8 tok/s / 2.37 accepted per round vs 3-bit draft head 55.4 / 2.19; the lever is defaulted off at block 5
forced-depth sweep 2026-08-20: 13.01 at depth 4 vs 10.78/9.63 at 5/6 (the verify width 6 cliff); auto at cap 6 measured 10.64 against --no-mtp's 10.57
saturated echo, median of 5, by forced depth: 3 47.44, 4 55.50, 5 47.50, 6 47.28; depth 4 is the only width where the cap binds, so no extension sync is paid

EV cost surface fit, MLX_SERVE_MTP_TRACE 2026-07-13, saturated fixed depths after the deferred-append round shape: T(1) 42.0, T(3) 62.6, T(6) 111.6, T(7) 114.9 ms; piecewise ~10.3 ms/pos to seq 4, ~16.3 ms/pos for 4-6, position 7 +3.3 ms; ~90% qmm row-count cost, GDN recurrence < 1 ms/round

Typical 0.2 plus the paired routed gate/up kernel over the exact control, 1K rung of the 1K-1M ladder; the ladder spans +16.2% (1K, Typical) to +27.0% (1M, TokenV3); 128K-1M points are one request per arm

llmprobe creative, thinking off, three timed samples, sampled drafts, MTP depth 3, short median: exact 92.5, Typical 0.2 106.3, TokenV3 0.95 106.5; opposite pack (MTPLX BF16 KV): 102.0 / 115.5 / 119.3
CLEARLY_WORSE motivation: w5 read 94.7 ms/tok against trusted w4's 71.2 on its first sample and never moved; at 3-samples-to-trust the bucket cost -7.1%

measured.model: GLM-5.3-Flash (sparse MoE, every extra row routes to more experts)

lab_mapping.maps_to: workload Speculation.adaptive and the TURBOSPARK_ADAPTIVE_DEPTH knob (crates/lab/src/knobs.rs:240), plus our AdaptiveDepth controller's cap
lab_mapping.note: our knob only changes which depth each round proposes and stays lossless, like their EV plan; their per-silicon cap rows are the shape our machine cap would take

lab_mapping.setting: round_cost_ema_beta and the drop rules, explore schedule, width_switch_margin
lab_mapping.note: their table is the live-measured cousin of our two modeled costs (67.5 and 129.5 ms); depth-replay's fixed-block arms can be read as their trial blocks
our tree-replay prices trees, not lookup or copied continuations; the tokens-per-cost gate is what our Kapitsa lever 5 replay would replace with a replay-priced table

notes: Doc-vs-source checks, sided with the source. (1) Our doc says a lookup round never feeds the EV or cost state; the source is narrower: a lookup round skips the EV acceptance EMAs, the grouped planner, and the width grid, and the MTP round after it is dropped too, but it DOES price the table's separate lookup row via observeLookup (src/generate.zig:7130). (2) Our doc's 8 on NAX is exact only for the five calibrated NAX quant surfaces; the dense 27B q4/gs64 surface and both qwen4 surfaces keep 6 on M5 because their measured marginals never pay past depth 6 (src/generate.zig:10787-10793). (3) Our doc's 6 off NAX is the generic-surface default; M1 Pro, base M4, and base M5 carry measured cold-start rows of 4, and an explicit --mtp-max-depth overrides all rows. (4) The doc's per-draft acceptance gate at 50% after 5 rounds matches RUNTIME_GATE_MIN_PER_DRAFT_RATE and RUNTIME_GATE_WARMUP; note the EV controller replaces that gate's demote path post-warmup and keeps only a sticky depth-1 floor at 0.20 over a homogeneous 16-round window. (5) The M4 block-sweep source comment names the chip only as applegpu_g16s and the model as Muse 4-bit; Muse-Glimmer 30B and M4 Max are our naming. (6) Doc claims with no line at this rev, kept out of measured: the 1.63x to 2.04x Flash Next cross-request seed ratio, the 11 of 19 agent runs cut by the lookup loop guard, the 0.03 ms emit gap, and the block-5 round profile (verify 50.2 ms, assistant 6.2, head 2.9, append 0.9, accept 0.2, gap 0.01). (7) The lookup gate's verifyCost fit was fitted on an M5 Ultra and only prices rounds where the table has no measurement yet; its numbers are not machine-portable. (8) Lookup caps are additionally held to an explicit --mtp-max-depth via depth_bounds.lookupCap (src/mtp_depth_bounds.zig:61). (9) dflash_policy.zig is the sparse-target (GLM-5.3-Flash class) round policy where a verify row is not free; on the dense 27B the row cost is flat and the WidthChooser / EV plan run instead.
